stem: A nurse teaches a client how to check moles for warning signs of melanoma. Which assessment follows the ABCDE approach?

options.A: Assess only whether a lesion is painful and ignore visible changes.
options.B: Assess asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, and whether the lesion is evolving.
options.C: Assess only lesion color because size, shape, and change over time are not useful warning signs.
options.D: Assess only lesions larger than 6 mm and ignore smaller lesions even when they are changing.

rationale: The American Academy of Dermatology describes the ABCDE warning signs of melanoma as Asymmetry, irregular or poorly defined Border, varying Color, Diameter, and Evolving change. Although melanomas are often larger than 6 mm when diagnosed, they can be smaller, so diameter is not an absolute cutoff. B is the only option that accurately applies the full ABCDE approach.
educational_objective: Teach clients to use the ABCDE approach to recognize skin lesions that warrant professional evaluation for possible melanoma.
source_document_title: Melanoma: Signs and symptoms — The ABCDEs of melanoma
source_version_date: Current AAD web guidance; currentness rechecked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Section: The ABCDEs of melanoma — A Asymmetry; B Border; C Color; D Diameter; E Evolving
source_claim_supported: AAD identifies asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, and evolving change as melanoma warning signs; melanoma can be smaller than 6 mm.

source_original.stem: A nurse is teaching a client how to perform a skin self-exam to check moles for potential skin cancer warning signs. The nurse should teach the client the "ABCDE" mnemonic, which includes checking for:

options.A: Assess only whether the lesion is painful and ignore its visible characteristics
options.B: Assess asymmetry, border, color, diameter, and whether the lesion is evolving
options.C: Assess only lesion color because size and symmetry are not useful warning signs
options.D: Assess only lesions larger than six millimeters and ignore changes over time

source_original.rationale: The ABCDE mnemonic for skin self-exams teaches clients to check moles for: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variation (multiple colors within one mole), Diameter greater than about 6mm, and Evolving characteristics (any change in size, shape, or color over time) — all warning signs that should prompt further evaluation by a healthcare provider.
source_original.source_detail: ABCDE warning signs: asymmetry, border, color, diameter, evolving; current page, accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Kept the correct ABCDE construct, tightened the stem and distractors, and corrected the rationale so 6 mm is not treated as an absolute threshold because AAD explicitly notes melanoma can be smaller.

audit_findings.source_authority: AAD current clinical patient guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan for blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: AAD melanoma signs page was current and accessible on 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Every component of ABCDE was directly verified; the source also explicitly states melanoma may be smaller than 6 mm.

distractor_audit.A: Pain alone is not the ABCDE method.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrectly converts diameter into an absolute exclusion threshold and ignores evolving change.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B includes all five ABCDE domains without adding an unsupported exclusion rule.
audit_findings.cueing: Options are parallel assessment strategies; the key depends on melanoma-screening knowledge.
audit_findings.blueprint: Preventive self-assessment teaching maps to Health Promotion and Maintenance.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked the AAD ABCDE page, specifically the diameter nuance and evolving criterion; no second correct answer remained.
